en.intro: I help teams see how they act, communicate, and respond to one another in concrete situations.
en.proof: DISC as a model, not a personality test.

sections.heading: DISC without myths
sections.intro: Plain language instead of diagnosis and fixed labels.

items.title: A model of behavioural styles and communication
items.body: DISC describes preferred ways of acting and communicating. It is not a clinical diagnosis or a fixed label.

sections.heading: Who it is for and which problems it helps
sections.intro: The training is for teams that want to understand how they work and talk about collaboration more clearly.

items.title: Different communication styles
items.body: A shared language helps identify where misunderstandings in everyday cooperation come from.

items.title: Pace, decisions, and responsibility
items.body: Different preferences can become a constructive topic instead of a source of quick judgement.

items.title: Feedback
items.body: Participants examine how to express needs clearly and listen to people who respond differently.

items.title: A shared language for cooperation
items.body: The model gives a team language for discussing behaviour without reducing people to one type.

sections.heading: What the training can support
sections.intro: Training does not change a team for its participants. It offers language, observations, and exercises that can support everyday collaboration.

items.title: Recognizing preferences
items.body: The team notices different ways of responding and acting.

items.title: Adapting communication
items.body: Participants practise speaking clearly to people with different needs.

items.title: A shared language for cooperation
items.body: Differences can be discussed without judgement or diagnosis.

sections.heading: What the training looks like
sections.intro: We start with the team's goal, not with a ready-made label. Then we work through the model, examples, and practical reflection.

items.title: Team goal and context
items.body: We start with a situation that matters to participants.

items.title: DISC concepts
items.body: We make the model practical and easy to use.

items.title: Exercises and observations
items.body: Examples make behaviour visible in action.

items.title: Transfer to collaboration
items.body: We finish with insights for everyday conversations.

sections.heading: Music, boomwhackers, and DISC
sections.intro: When the team's goal calls for it, music and boomwhackers create an experience that opens a conversation about listening, response, and collaboration.

items.title: Experiencing difference without labels
items.body: A shared rhythm makes group behaviour visible, while reflection connects it to communication.

items.title: MaxiDISC
items.body: Consultant certificate after training, mentoring, and an exam.

items.title: Practical group work
items.body: Experience since 2010 and contexts described in sources.

sections.intro: Format, duration, group size, and pricing depend on the team's goal. We agree the details after a short conversation.

items.title: Format
items.body: DISC team training with an optional music-based variant.

items.title: Teams, leaders, HR, and L&D
items.body: The scope is matched to the team's situation and the goal participants bring to the session.

items.body: Agreed individually with the programme, group size, venue, and logistics in mind.

faq.question: Is DISC a personality test?
faq.answer: No. It is a model of communication and cooperation styles, not a clinical diagnosis or fixed label.

faq.question: Which teams is the training for?
faq.answer: Teams, leaders, HR, and L&D. The scope depends on the team's situation.

faq.question: Does the training have to include boomwhackers?
faq.answer: No. The music variant is optional and used only when it supports the team's goal.

faq.question: How long does the training take?
faq.answer: It depends on the goal, group size, and programme.

faq.question: How do we agree on price?
faq.answer: Individually, after a short conversation about needs, scope, timing, and logistics.
